messages:
maria: FYI, after the RBAC tweaks this morning the SCIM sync to AcmeCorp started failing. Seeing a bunch of KMS decrypt errors and then OIDC introspect returning 429s. Anyone seen this pattern before? :eyes:
kevin: On it. Can you paste the logs?
ajay: Might be a KMS key policy or role permission issue if decrypt fails after a deploy. Also could be transient KMS throttling.
maria: Logs: ```
2025-02-15T14:02:10Z ERROR scim.sync: user_import failed id=acct-1123 decrypt err=kms.Decrypt error: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded
2025-02-15T14:02:11Z WARN oidc.client: token_introspect HTTP 429, Retry-After: 30s
2025-02-15T14:02:12Z ERROR scim.sync: batch 42 aborted due to decrypt failure
```
sophia: Hmm — two simultaneous failure modes. If KMS decrypt is timing out, the SCIM job will abort and might flood the IDP with retries, triggering introspect rate limits. Could be a retry storm.
kevin: I checked KMS metrics in the last 2h, there's a spike of throttles around 14:01-14:05. No recent key rotation in our audit logs but there was an RBAC permissions change on the SCIM service role at 13:58.
ajay: Can you confirm the SCIM service principal still has kms:Decrypt on the key alias we use? Also check whether the request context includes the encryption context we expect (tenant:acmecorp). Missed ctx can cause failures.
maria: IAM policy snippet we applied: ```json
{"Effect":"Allow","Action":["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt"],"Resource":"arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01"}```
kevin: That looks okay at first glance. But the RBAC change also removed a wildcard condition that added the encryptionContext requirement. The KMS key has a key policy that requires an EncryptionContext key "tenant". If the caller stopped sending it, decrypt will fail silently or timeout.
sophia: Also confirm VPC endpoints/NAT for KMS are healthy. We had a brief egress issue earlier today which could explain deadline exceeded. ops-bot: Alert: we observed 502/504 spikes for scim-sync-prod around 14:00 (aggregate 1m error rate +250%).
maria: Good call. I can repro locally with a small script that omits EncryptionContext and see the same error. Test script: ```bash
curl -X POST "https://scim.redwood.internal/sync" -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"tenant":"acmecorp","users":[...]}'}
```
kevin: Immediate mitigation options: 1) Add client-side exponential backoff with jitter for KMS calls and OIDC introspect. 2) Add a short circuit so failed decrypts don't immediately retry the entire batch. 3) Temporarily route SCIM traffic to secondary key (if available) or switch to cached tokens to reduce introspect load.
ajay: For the long term: ensure encryptionContext is part of the signing/integration test suite, add a pre-flight check in the SCIM worker that validates decrypts at batch start, and add quota-aware introspect client that respects Retry-After headers.
sophia: I'll open a quick runbook: check key policy, check caller encryption context, check VPC endpoint health, and monitor KMS Throttles metric. If KMS throttles > 100/min for 5m, escalate to infra.
maria: Action items: @kevin verify service role permissions + encryptionContext in outgoing requests (assigned). @ajay update client to exponential backoff + honor Retry-After (P0). @sophia open runbook and monitor (P1). I'll notify AcmeCorp SSO admin that we're investigating. :thumbsup:
kevin: Done — found that the SCIM worker library lost a header due to a refactor. Pushed hotfix to reattach the encryptionContext header. Redeploying to prod canary now.
oncall-bot: Deploy started by kevin at 2025-02-15T14:18:03Z — canary to 3 pods.
maria: Canary logs look clean so far, no decrypt errors in the last 5m and introspect 429s dropped to baseline. Monitoring for 30m then rollback plan if issues. :relieved:
ops-bot: Note: created incident page INC-20250215-73 and linked runbook.
ajay: Follow-up todo: add unit test that fails if encryptionContext is missing, and add integration test for introspect rate-limit handling.
maria: Thanks team. Will keep this thread updated if anything regresses.
